lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Donna! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Here's what I had in mind for today, but tell me if you'd rather focus on something else.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about what to eat at parties.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Tired, but okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My arms feel stronger already.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, if I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could you do them while you watch TV?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the band exercises going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're really honest with yourself, and that helps.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the band exercises. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I need this for my head too, not just my body. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that getting started keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, let's say I do the band exercises 5 times.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: 7. Maybe 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 7 and not a 4?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can do the band while I watch my novela.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If it rains I'll walk in the hallway of my building.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to do the band exercises 5 times. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Asks about party eating; coach does not follow up
Sidesteps the participant's stated party question
Expresses need and guilt; coach does not reflect it
States desire to feel like self; coach does not reflect it
Leading suggestion framed as question; participant declines

flags.reason: Participant voiced need and guilt about cancer returning; coach replied with a generic autonomy line instead of reflecting it.
Participant said 'I really want to feel like myself again'; coach moved to a TV-suggestion question without reflecting the desire.
Coach offered a specific solution (exercise during TV) framed as a question before exploring the barrier; participant declined.
Participant's stated question about party eating was not acknowledged or revisited.
'It's completely your call' is used four times (lines 12, 28, 42, 53), feeling formulaic and reducing its effect.

score.summary: The coach elicited a concrete, self-chosen goal (band exercises five times) and checked confidence and barriers well, ending with an accurate summary and next contact. Empathy and responsiveness were uneven: several clear change statements (lines 11, 23) were met with generic autonomy lines or a leading question instead of reflection.
strengths: Line 37: 'Why is this important to you right now?' elicited the participant's own values and reasons.
Line 54-56: The confidence scale followed by 'Why a 7 and not a 4?' built on the participant's self-efficacy.
Line 60: Clear summary of the plan with a check for accuracy, then a concrete next contact at line 62.
coaching_tips: Line 11: Reflect the participant's stated need ('You want to stay well for yourself and your family') before moving to planning.
Line 23: Reflect the desire 'to feel like myself again' rather than moving straight to a TV suggestion.
Line 24: Ask permission or explore the barrier first ('Would it help to talk through what gets in the way on Sundays?').
Line 5: Acknowledge the party-food question and agree on whether to address it, so the participant's agenda is honored.
Lines 12, 28, 42, 53: Vary the autonomy language and pair it with a reflection to avoid sounding scripted.
